questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How the film 'Jaws' was made in the 1970s
Sharks' scary image, the facts, and human threats
How to stay safe when swimming in the sea
Why sharks are becoming more dangerous to humans
questions.why: They explain that sharks' fearsome reputation isn't based on facts, and that humans kill millions of sharks.

questions.q: According to Sam, why do most shark attacks on humans happen?
options: Sharks are very hungry in the summer months
Sharks want revenge on people who hunt them
Swimmers go too far away from the beach
The shark thinks the swimmer is a fish
questions.why: Sam says most attacks are cases of mistaken identity, where the shark mistakes a swimmer for fish.

questions.q: In recent years, how many people a year have died from shark bites worldwide, on average?
options: About four hundred
About forty
About four
About four thousand
questions.why: Sam says the average annual number of deaths from shark bites was as low as four.

questions.q: How many sharks are caught and killed by humans each year?
options: Over 100 million
About 530
Around 400,000
questions.why: Sam says over 100 million sharks are caught and killed each year.

questions.q: What does George Burgess think of the shark in 'Jaws'?
options: It shows quite well how great whites behave
It is completely unlike real sharks
It is realistic, but the attacks are too bloody
It helped people understand sharks better
questions.why: He says the idea of a shark with a grudge chasing humans – 'nothing could be further from the truth'.

questions.q: What does Rob say about how long sharks have existed?
options: They appeared after the dinosaurs died out
They have changed a lot in the last million years
They first appeared about 4 million years ago
They're older than dinosaurs, almost unchanged
questions.why: Rob says they have hardly changed in 400 million years, making them older than the dinosaurs.

questions.q: According to Oliver Crimmin, what is special about a shark's skeleton?
options: It has no bone, so it's light and flexible
It is made of very heavy and strong bones
It is larger than any other fish's skeleton
It grows back quickly when it is damaged
questions.why: He says there's no bone in the skeleton, and this flexible material makes sharks agile and lightweight.

questions.q: Why does Sam tell listeners to feel the fold of their ear?
options: To show how sharks are able to hear sounds
To explain how sharks lose their fins
So they can feel what cartilage is like
To show that humans have no cartilage
questions.why: After Rob explains cartilage, Sam says to feel the fold of your ear – 'that's cartilage'.
